before: \label{sec:3d-method} \label{sec:eavail-definition} Truth available energy is defined by its implementation, for which ``low-recoil convention'' is shorthand. In MeV, the truth function (\texttt{CVUniverse::GetEAvailableTrue()}) computes \begin{equation}  E_{\rm avail}^{\rm true}=  \sum_{p}(E-938.27)  +\sum_{\pi^\pm}(E-135)  +\sum_{\pi^0}E  +\sum_{\gamma}E .  \label{eq:eavail-implemented} \end{equation} Protons and charged pions contribute the indicated kinetic-energy-like terms; neutral pions and photons contribute total energy. All other final-state species contribute zero, including neutrons, the primary muon, secondary $e^\pm$, neutrinos, kaons, antiprotons, strange baryons, other mesons and nuclear-remnant records. Reconstructed available energy is the MAT calorimetric quantity \begin{equation}  E_{\rm avail}^{\rm reco}=1.17\left[(E_{\rm blob}^{\rm tracker}  -E_{\mu\text{-fuzz}}^{\rm tracker})+(E_{\rm blob}^{\rm ECAL}  -E_{\mu\text{-fuzz}}^{\rm ECAL})\right],  \label{eq:eavail-reco-implemented} \end{equation} implemented in the reconstruction function (\texttt{CVUniverse::NewEavail()}), with no final clamp to non-negative values.

before: \label{sec:method-config} \paragraph{The estimator configurations.} Six estimator configurations, labeled (a)--(f), are used; Table~\ref{tab:estimators-matrix} gives each one's learner, background treatment and results, and each result names the configuration it uses. All use five OmniFold iterations and gradient-boosted trees of nominal capacity (100 trees, 8 leaves) in both OmniFold steps; ``deterministic'' means fixed seeds and reproducible training. Results from different configurations are not combined. Four are described in this section: \begin{itemize}[itemsep=1pt, topsep=2pt]   \item (f), the nominal LightGBM configuration above with refined negative-weight subtraction and the refinement classifier of (e), seeded at the estimator seed plus three: the 2D central value (seed~42) and its uncertainty ensembles (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:results});   \item (a), the same learner with purity-based background subtraction (Sec.~\ref{sec:method-algo}): the five-dimensional central value (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:eavailw}), the 3D and 4D injected-bump closures and Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:eavail-marg} and~Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:q3excess} (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:3d}), and the purity-subtracted 2D comparisons of Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:results-tension};   \item (e), the joint-test estimator: a deterministic LightGBM variant with the unbinned negative-weight background treatment (App.~\ref{app:negweight}), whose refinement classifier has 400 trees and 31 leaves. The negative-weight treatment reduces the purity method's nominal-truth bias in the highest-$W$ column at least fifteen-fold (from \SIrange{3.5}{4.1}{\percent} to \SIrange{0.11}{0.24}{\percent}, the level of the no-background closure), and the larger refinement classifier removes most of the background-related bias that remains (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-negweight}--Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}). It gives the 3D and 4D central values (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:3d}) and the sixteen-cell five-dimensional result (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:fived16}). It is used for the generator tests (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d}), the study of generator shapes held out of its development (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}) and the precision study (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:gbdt-model-dependence}). It was selected before the joint-test design was fixed (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d});   \item (b), the exact-split cross-check above. \end{itemize} Configuration (c) is the deterministic variant with purity-based subtraction, and (d) is the same variant with negative weights and a nominal-capacity refinement; they serve the background-bias, generator-sized-change and coverage studies listed in the table. The five-dimensional central value of Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:eavailw} and its five-axis covariance use configuration~(a): they were produced before the purity bias was found and the refinement was developed. A refined five-dimensional data unfolding (configuration~(e)) gives the sixteen-cell result; its reported covariance on the sixteen cells is described in Sec.~\ref{sec:fived16-cov}. The 2D central value and its covariance were rebuilt with configuration~(f) after a two-dimensional closure test with backgrounds found the purity bias (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, App.~\ref*{N-sec:negweight-footing}). The change was decided on that closure test, before the rebuilt result's distance from the published result was computed, and the rebuilt result was adopted after that distance was known. The exact-split central value was the quoted 2D central value until 2026-10-11; studies labeled \emph{exact-split} use it and have not been recomputed. The 3D and 4D central values have been regenerated with configuration~(e); no 3D or 4D covariance is quoted.

before: \label{sec:joint5d-calibration} The null distribution of each statistic is obtained from pseudo-experiments that run the full analysis chain at the null truth, using the joint-test estimator (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}). That estimator is deterministic LightGBM OmniFold with five iterations and the negative-weight background treatment, whose refinement classifier has 400 trees and 31 leaves. Each pseudo-experiment \begin{itemize}[itemsep=1pt, topsep=2pt]   \item draws Poisson pseudo-data from one half of the simulation together with an independent background source, refits the background-refinement classifier, and unfolds with the estimator trained on the other half;   \item draws one of \jtFluxUniverses{} flux universes and every one of the \jtModelBands{} interaction-model bands at one of its universes;   \item draws the weight-based detector bands (MINOS muon-matching efficiency and the GEANT4 neutron, pion and proton interaction reweights) and the five muon and beam-angle lateral bands through a linear surrogate;   \item draws a \SI{1.4}{\percent} normalization, the data's rounding noise (taken from 20 real-data re-unfolds with rounding-level input changes), and the prediction's finite-sample residual. \end{itemize} The data are unfolded once, with the full simulation. The Monte Carlo $p$ value of a test is $(k+1)/(B+1)$, where $k$ of $B$ null pseudo-experiments reach the observed statistic. This $p$ value is never zero. The $p$ value on which each decision rests, the \emph{claim} $p$ value, is the largest over the declared \emph{claim variants}, which shift the null. The variants move it by an upper bound on the simulation-size difference between the pseudo-experiments and the data unfold (condition~(iv) below), and by $\pm\jtMoneKappa\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$ (condition~(i)). The external nulls are strongly non-central, with non-centralities $\lambda$ of \jtLambdaMin{}--\jtLambdaMax{} in these units. They are non-central because the calibration reproduces the estimator's pull toward its prior (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}). Each observed statistic is compared with that displaced distribution (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:joint5d-nulls}).

before: \label{sec:method-config} \paragraph{The estimator configurations.} The analysis uses six estimator configurations, labeled (a)--(f); Table~\ref{tab:estimators-matrix} lists their learners, background treatments and results. Each result identifies its configuration. All use five OmniFold iterations and gradient-boosted trees of nominal capacity (100 trees, 8 leaves) in both OmniFold steps; ``deterministic'' means fixed seeds and reproducible training. Results from different configurations are not combined. Four are described in this section: \begin{itemize}[itemsep=1pt, topsep=2pt]   \item (f), the nominal LightGBM configuration above with refined negative-weight subtraction and the refinement classifier of (e), seeded at the estimator seed plus three: the 2D central value (seed~42) and its uncertainty ensembles (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:results});   \item (a), the same learner with purity-based background subtraction (Sec.~\ref{sec:method-algo}): the five-dimensional central value (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:eavailw}), the 3D and 4D injected-bump closures and Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:eavail-marg} and~Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:q3excess} (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:3d}), and the purity-subtracted 2D comparisons of Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:results-tension};   \item (e), the five-observable estimator (the joint-test estimator of Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}): a deterministic LightGBM variant with the unbinned negative-weight background treatment (App.~\ref{app:negweight}), whose refinement classifier has 400 trees and 31 leaves. The negative-weight treatment reduces the purity method's nominal-truth bias in the highest-$W$ column at least fifteen-fold (from \SIrange{3.5}{4.1}{\percent} to \SIrange{0.11}{0.24}{\percent}, the level of the no-background closure), and the larger refinement classifier removes most of the background-related bias that remains (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-negweight}--Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}). It gives the 3D and 4D central values (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:3d}) and the sixteen-cell five-dimensional result (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:fived16}). It is used for the generator tests (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d}), the study of generator shapes held out of its development (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:val-departure}) and the precision study (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:gbdt-model-dependence}). It was selected before the joint-test design was fixed (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d});   \item (b), the exact-split cross-check above. \end{itemize} Configuration (c) is the deterministic variant with purity-based subtraction, and (d) is the same variant with negative weights and a nominal-capacity refinement; they are used in the background-bias, generator-sized-change and coverage studies listed in the table. The five-dimensional central value of Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:eavailw} and its five-axis covariance use configuration~(a): they were produced before the purity bias was found and the refinement was developed. A refined five-dimensional data unfolding (configuration~(e)) gives the sixteen-cell result; its reported covariance on the sixteen cells is described in Sec.~\ref{sec:fived16-cov}. The 2D central value and its covariance were rebuilt with configuration~(f) after a two-dimensional closure test with backgrounds found the purity bias (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, App.~\ref*{N-sec:negweight-footing}). The closure test determined the change before the distance between the rebuilt and published results was computed. The rebuilt result was adopted after that distance was known. The exact-split central value was the quoted 2D central value in an earlier version of the analysis; studies labeled \emph{exact-split} use it and have not been recomputed. The 3D and 4D central values have been regenerated with configuration~(e); no 3D or 4D covariance is quoted.

before: Production uses $n=5$ iterations. Huang \emph{et al.}~\cite{Huang:2025omnifold} select 45 iterations for OmniFold-family methods (20 for their binned benchmark) using a binned $\chi^{2}$ against known mock-data truth, a criterion they note is infeasible on real data. We do not adopt that recommendation. Their mock data inject a large prior--data \emph{shape} discrepancy through an RPA-modified quasielastic model, requiring many iterations. The simulation prior differs from the measured distributions mainly in normalization: the data exceed it by about 12\%, and the data/MC ratio rises with $\pT$ from 0.88 to about 1.2 (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:controlplots}). Cross-experiment production also typically uses ${\sim}5$ iterations~\cite{Canelli:2025guide}. The checks support $n=5$: for the exact-split cross-check, the total cross section agrees to within \SI{0.026}{\percent} between five and ten iterations (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:validation}), and the unfolded result reproduces an independently published binned measurement of the same data (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:results}).
